content: Speak words that are pleasing and sweet; why speak harsh words when gentle words are freely available, like eating raw unripe fruit when ripe sweet fruit is right at hand? (Kural 99-100)
author: Thiruvalluvar
explanation:
In the Sangam masterpiece of the Tirukkural, Thiruvalluvar provides a universal ethical compass for integrating righteous duty (*Aram*), practical prosperity (*Porul*), and enduring human nobility.

This passage emphasizes the vital importance of speak and words in human life. By moving beyond superficial distractions and grounding attention in timeless ethical principles, we cultivate inner stability, clarity of thought, and genuine resilience.

True realization is never an abstract academic debate—it is an active discipline practiced through conscious daily choices and unwavering integrity.
